recipes.name: Easy, Cheesy Tortellini Bake
ingredients_raw: 1 (10 ounce) box frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed dry

steps.text: Preheat the oven broiler; adjust an oven rack to the highest position. Generously butter or grease an 8x8-inch baking dish.
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add tortellini and cook according to package directions; drain and set aside.
Bring marinara and Alfredo sauces, spinach, and 1 tablespoon Italian seasoning to a simmer in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir tortellini into sauce, then pour into the prepared baking dish. Sprinkle with mozzarella cheese, Parmesan cheese, and 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning.
Broil until cheese has melted and turned golden brown, 1 to 2 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy, Cheesy Tortellini Bake
raw_recipe.description: This delicious easy cheesy tortellini bake comes out of the oven golden brown and sizzling in just 30 minutes! Your guests will think you spent hours on it.

review.reviewBody: Like many other reviewers, I added extra tortellini. In fact, I tripled it. I bought 2 19oz packages of frozen tortellini and used 1 1/2 of them. I used the same amounts of sauce, but rinsed the jars with a couple oz of water which I mixed in. I also baked the tortellini for about 20 minutes at 350 degrees F covered, then added the cheese on top and baked about 10 more minutes uncovered. This is a very tasty dish. Hubby thought there was too much "green stuff", but I really liked the spinach. It's all in your taste.

This is definitely a 5-star recipe for me. I used a 20 oz. pkg. of cheese tortellini,low fat alfredo sauce, and a jar of pasta sauce with Italian sausage, peppers, and onions because that is what I had on hand in the pantry. Since I don't like the texture of frozen spinach, I used a 6 oz.package of fresh spinach. I divided the recipe between 2, 8 x 8 inch pans-one to bake and one to freeze (without the cheese) and bake later. I also did not broil the tortellini. Instead, I placed the uncovered casserole dish in a 350 degree oven and baked until the sauce started to bubble and the cheese turned golden brown. Each 8 x 8 inch pan serves 4. This recipe is a keeper!

I was a little unsure how this would taste but it was really good! I used hot italian sausage that I browned with onion and garlic. I used about 3/4 lb fresh spinach (instead of frozen -- tastes better, not as overpowering as frozen), and 19 oz of cheese tortellini (cooked). I mixed it all together with the sauces and 1 T. Italian seasoning spice mix in a large pan on medium heat until the sauces were blended and the fresh spinach was slightly wilted. I put it in an 11x13 pan, sprinkled a little less than one cup of shredded Italian cheese blend on top (omitted the extra seasoning), baked at 350 degrees for about 30 minutes and then broiled for about 3 minutes. Served with garlic bread. Very tasty. With the sausage, 19 oz of tortellini and the fresh spinach, the sauce ratio was perfect.

This recipe is great!, quick and easy; however, I modified it some. I added 2 chicken breast by cutting the meat into small cubes. I added the Italian seasoning (less than 1/2 amount req'd br recipe), salt & black pepper to chicken, cooked in olive oil and skillet. I also added 1/2 box of Barilla, Mostaccioli, boil water and lightly salt before adding Mostaccioli. Then I mixed the Marinia Sauce & Alfredo Sauce (Three Cheeses) and spinach and added it to the drained tortellini. I let all of this come to a boil, stirring frequently to avoid sticking. Then sprayed Olive oil into a 9x11 glass pan, spooned the mixture into the glass pan leaving room for other layers. Cover the mixture with a layer of Mozzarolla cheese and a layer of parmesan cheese repeat until pan is full. Bake 350* for ~50 minutes. The top layer of cheese will turn a nice golden brown. I wish that I had taken a picture, but didn't know that I could add one. Yummy!! My family loved it and so did I.

We enjoyed this a lot, but too much sauce for the recommended pasta. I used 2 - 19 oz pkgs of tortellini, a 9 x 13 dish, baked covered for 20 minutes at 350, and uncovered for 10 minutes. I'll brown a pound of bulk sausage next time to add to the casserole.

I sauteed hot Italian sausage, onions and bell peppers then added the sauces, spinach and Italian seasoning. I also added salt, pepper and garlic powder. My box of frozen spinach was 8 oz and that was plenty. I added the tortellini and simmered for about 10 minutes. I saw no reason to bake it so I just put a lid on the saucepan and let the cheeses melted. Thanks for sharing your recipe.

Both my husband and I loved this. I was in a hurry, misread directions and ended up pouring the sauces directly from the jars into the pot of cooked and drained pasta to which I then added the spinach, Italian seasoning and freshly grated Parmesan cheese. I also added hot Italian sausage before topping it with fresh ground mozzarella (don't use packaged, it has cellulose ). I baked it for 20 min. At 400. My measurements were metric vs imperial so approximate. Despite my errors, this was yummy. I appreciated another reviewer's comments re difference in quality of jarred sauces which I don't usually use. I went on a google search and was very pleased to find Rao sauce (which got a very good rating) in a local grocery store. Will definitely make this again and look forward to making it properly. ??

I see this recipe has been posted for many years and the older reviews say that there was too much sauce. The recipe was later revised to increase the amount of tortellini. That being said, the ratio of sauce to tortellini was just right. It was excellent and I agree with many things the other reviewers wrote, such as the picture really does not do it justice, just baking it for 20 minutes and not bothering trying to broil it, cutting back a little on the spinach and use quality sauces. I added some leftover cut up meatballs and it was hit, you can see how there are many add in possibilities. Definitely will make again.

I just made this tonight using a 18 oz bag of Wal-Mart tortellini. I put it all in an 11x8 dish and it was the perfect size. I baked it at 350 for 20 minutes. Perfect! The sauce is a pink sauce which is commonly found in Italian restaurants. (tomato sauce with heavy cream added) That is what you get when you mix marinara and alfredo - a pink sauce. It is rich and creamy. This is a good base recipe which can easily handle added cooked ingredients such as chicken, sausage or shrimp. Easy, delicious and satisfying!

This turned out delicious using the listed ingredients but I did change the ratios. I used leftover meat sauce that I had made for a lasagna instead of spaghetti sauce. I mixed equal parts of alfredo and meat sauce, almost tripled the amount of tortellini and added some extra cheese on top using Trader Joes quattro formagio blend, in addition to the mozzarella and parmesan listed. Baked in a 9 x 13 pan.
This sounds good and would love to make it, however, what can I use besides spinach, since this family hates spinach?
Needed more spinach, switched cheezes, less broiler time. Basic recipe was filling and tasty.
I thought it was average but my fiancé thought it was amazing, fantastic, perfect, delicious, and on and on! Easy to make so I will definitely keep this in the rotation!

One of my go-to recipes when I need to make dinner last-minute. I have a nice meal ready in under an hour, and it looks and tastes more impressive than it actually is. I add a little more oregano and garlic.
This was really good, & easy. Yes I will make it again.

I came across this recipe a little while back and decided to give it a whirl, Well so glad I did my son who isn't much of a pasta eater absolutely loves this recipe & I do believe it's now up there with one of his favorite meals!!! That being said the only thing I add to this when I make it is bulk Italian sausage, I slice it in rings fry it up & mix it in & for a change up once in a while instead of using just regular alfredo I usually use garlic alfredo & it's perfect.
I made this a couple of times. Very easy and good!
Turns out great every time and everyone in my family loves it!

i used a 16 oz bag of tortellini and that was spot on. I didn't find it too soupy. I hate dry anything. I didn't place in broil just by choice so heated it in the oven. The sauce is what makes it imo, so if you're not a fan of spinach, add what you like. I'm not a fan of tortellini so i might combine spinach and ricotta then stuff shells and cover with sauce.
